original_question: For non-unique factorisations [[P,Q(P)]]=♦(P,[[P,P]]) of the Poisson-cocycle condition through Leibniz graphs, what is the topological structure of the resulting identities ♦₂−♦₁≡0? Equivalently, if one forms a meta-graph whose vertices are Leibniz graphs and where adjacency means that two Leibniz graphs have expansions sharing a Kontsevich oriented graph, what are the genus, diameter, typical cycle length, and related invariants of these meta-graphs, and how does the iterative generation algorithm saturate them?
target_in_paper: The draft is targeting the paper’s unnumbered open problem about the non-uniqueness of factorisations of the Poisson cocycle condition through Leibniz graphs, and the resulting “nontrivial topology” of the induced Leibniz meta-graph of such factorisations. The paper’s scope is explicitly combinatorial/topological on the graph side, not a request for specific numerical graph invariants such as genus or diameter. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the relevant factorisation problem [[P,Q(P)]] = ♦(P,[[P,P]]), the role of Leibniz graphs, the fact that distinct factorisations can lead to identities of the form (♦2-♦1)(P,[[P,P]]) ≡ 0, and the useful meta-graph viewpoint in which Leibniz graphs are connected when their expansions share an oriented Kontsevich graph. It also correctly notices the iterative saturation procedure used to generate candidate Leibniz graphs. ([rburing.nl](https://www.rburing.nl/gcaops/gcaops-dissertation-rburing.pdf))
missing_details: The ambient setting should be stated: P is a Poisson bi-vector on a finite-dimensional affine real manifold M, and Q(P) is the Kontsevich graph flow attached to a graph cocycle γ. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844))
The source of Q(P) should be made explicit: Q(P)=Or(γ)(P^{⊗ n}) for a graph cocycle γ on n vertices and 2n−2 edges. ([rburing.nl](https://www.rburing.nl/gcaops/gcaops-dissertation-rburing.pdf))

The factorisation problem should be stated in its paper-faithful form: [[P,Q(P)]] = ♦(P,[[P,P]]), i.e. the cocycle condition is factorised through the Jacobiator [[P,P]] by a sum of Leibniz graphs. ([rburing.nl](https://www.rburing.nl/gcaops/gcaops-dissertation-rburing.pdf))

The meaning of “Leibniz graph” should be included: it is a graph carrying one Jacobiator/trivector vertex [[P,P]] and otherwise Kontsevich-type aerial vertices, expanded by Leibniz rules into oriented Kontsevich graphs. ([rburing.nl](https://www.rburing.nl/gcaops/gcaops-dissertation-rburing.pdf))

The paper-faithful open problem is to study the resulting nontrivial topology/combinatorics of this Leibniz meta-graph; it does not single out genus, diameter, typical cycle length, or other chosen invariants as the main target. Those are your additions. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844))

If the meta-graph is used, its adjacency should be defined exactly: two Leibniz graphs are adjacent when their expansions have at least one oriented Kontsevich graph in common; multiple edges are allowed. ([rburing.nl](https://www.rburing.nl/gcaops/gcaops-dissertation-rburing.pdf))

The iterative generation algorithm should be described only as auxiliary context: starting from the Kontsevich expansion of [[P,Q(P)]], one iteratively adds Leibniz graphs whose expansions reproduce already known Kontsevich graphs, continuing until saturation/stabilization. ([rburing.nl](https://www.rburing.nl/gcaops/gcaops-dissertation-rburing.pdf))

No homogeneity assumption, polynomial degree restriction, nilpotency condition, characteristic assumption, or phrase such as ‘for all sufficiently large m’ belongs to this particular open problem. Those details are not part of the nearby statement. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844))
refined_question: Let P be a Poisson bi-vector on a finite-dimensional affine real manifold M, and let Q(P)=Or(γ)(P^{⊗ n}) be the Kontsevich infinitesimal symmetry determined by a graph cocycle γ on n vertices and 2n−2 edges. In the factorisation problem for the Poisson cocycle condition, [[P,Q(P)]] = ♦(P,[[P,P]]), where ♦ is expressed as a sum of Leibniz graphs, distinct factorising operators ♦1≠♦2 can occur, yielding identities (♦1−♦2)(P,[[P,P]]) ≡ 0. What is the resulting nontrivial topology/combinatorial structure of the Leibniz meta-graph whose vertices are Leibniz graphs (with one Jacobiator vertex) and whose adjacency is defined by sharing at least one oriented Kontsevich graph in their expansions? ([rburing.nl](https://www.rburing.nl/gcaops/gcaops-dissertation-rburing.pdf))
justification: The nearest paper-faithful target is not a request to compute particular graph invariants, but the narrower open problem of understanding the topology/combinatorics created by non-unique Leibniz-graph factorisations of the Poisson cocycle condition. The arXiv record states that the paper formulates open problems about combinatorial and topological properties of the graphs involved. A later authorial exposition makes the relevant content explicit: one constructs a saturated family of Leibniz graphs for [[P,Q(P)]], finds multiple solutions for ♦, and interprets the identities coming from ♦1−♦2 as evidence of a nontrivial Leibniz meta-graph whose study is open. Your draft is therefore aimed at the right local problem, but it broadens it by prescribing specific invariants (genus, diameter, typical cycle length, etc.) that the paper itself does not privilege. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.05844))
